title: The OODA Loop: How Fighter Pilots and Smart Leaders Make Better Decisions
author: The Good Boss
summary: The OODA loop—Observe, Orient, Decide, Act—is a decision framework borrowed from fighter pilot training that applies to leadership under uncertainty. The leader who observes conditions quickly, uses past knowledge to orient to the situation, decides rapidly, and acts decisively gains a competitive advantage. In business, just as in air combat, the side that cycles through the loop fastest while maintaining accuracy wins. The slowest decision-maker is not always the most careful; sometimes the slowest decision-maker is just slow.
points: Speed of decision-making matters more than perfect information; good decision-makers cycle through observe-orient-decide-act rapidly.
Orientation—the ability to interpret new information in light of experience and context—is the hidden lever that separates excellent decision-makers from merely competent ones.
The fear of being wrong slows leaders' decision cycles; accepting that some decisions will be adjusted post-action keeps the loop moving.
quotes: The person who can observe, orient, decide, and act faster than their competitor wins, even if their first decision is not perfect.
Perfectionism in decision-making is a liability, not a virtue. The virtue is speed with course-correction.” Archived from The Good Boss on April 21, 2026 by Tim.
